claim: Mobile robotics is a subfield of robotics and information engineering.
quote: Mobile robotics is usually considered to be a subfield of robotics and information engineering.

claim: Autonomous mobile robots can navigate uncontrolled environments without guidance devices.
quote: Mobile robots can be "autonomous" (AMR - autonomous mobile robot) which means they are capable of navigating an uncontrolled environment without the need for physical or electro-mechanical guidance devices.

claim: Mobile robots are used in commercial, industrial, military, and security settings.
quote: Mobile robots are also found in industrial, military and security settings.

claim: Mobile robots are equipped with controllers, sensors, actuators, and power systems.
quote: The components of a mobile robot are a controller, sensors, actuators and power system.

claim: Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) describes wireless communication between a vehicle and any entity that may affect, or may be affected by, the vehicle.
quote: Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) describes wireless communication between a vehicle and any entity that may affect, or may be affected by, the vehicle.

claim: V2X is intended to improve road safety and traffic efficiency while reducing pollution and saving energy.
quote: it is a vehicular communication system that is intended to improve road safety and traffic efficiency while reducing pollution and saving energy.

claim: There are two standards for dedicated V2X communications: WLAN-based and cellular-based.
quote: There are two standards for dedicated V2X communications depending on the underlying wireless technology being used: (1) WLAN-based, and (2) cellular-based.

claim: Vehicle-to-device (V2D) involves Bluetooth or WiFi-Direct communication, such as Apple's CarPlay and Google's Android Auto.
quote: Vehicle-to-device (V2D) - Bluetooth / WiFi-Direct, e.g. Apple's CarPlay and Google's Android Auto.

claim: Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) involves information exchange with the smart grid to balance loads more efficiently.
quote: Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) - information exchange with the smart grid to balance loads more efficiently.

claim: Vehicle-to-network (V2N) includes communication between a vehicle and a wider network, such as a cellular network.
quote: Vehicle-to-network (V2N) - communication between a vehicle and a wider network, such as a cellular network.

claim: Vehicle-to-cloud (V2C) includes OTA updates and remote vehicle diagnostics.
quote: Vehicle-to-cloud (V2C) - e.g. OTA updates, remote vehicle diagnostics (DoIP).

claim: Vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) involves communication with traffic lights, lane markers, and parking meters.
quote: Vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) - e.g. traffic lights, lane markers and parking meters.

claim: Vehicle-to-pedestrian (V2P) communication is used for wheelchairs and bicycles, designating vulnerable road users (VRUs).
quote: Vehicle-to-pedestrian (V2P) - e.g. wheelchairs and bicycles, commonly also used to designate vulnerable road users (VRUs).

claim: Vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) involves real-time data exchange with nearby vehicles.
quote: Vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) - real-time data exchange with nearby vehicles.

claim: Lane departure warning systems (LDWS) are designed to warn drivers when a vehicle begins to move out of its lane.
quote: a lane departure warning system ( LDWS ) is a mechanism designed to warn the driver when the vehicle begins to move out of its lane.

claim: Lane departure warning systems can use video, laser, and infrared sensors to detect lane markings.
quote: Lane warning/keeping systems are based on: Video sensors... Laser sensors... Infrared sensors...

claim: Lane keeping assist systems can automatically take steps to keep a vehicle in its lane if the driver does not respond to warnings.
quote: Lane keeping assist (LKA/LKS): Systems which warn the driver and, with no response, automatically take steps to ensure the vehicle stays in its lane.

claim: Automated lane keeping systems (ALKS) are designed to follow lane markings without human intervention.
quote: Automated lane keeping systems (ALKS): Designed to follow lane markings with no human driver.

claim: Lane departure warning systems may not function if lane edges are not marked by lines.
quote: This system does not work when the edge of the lane is not marked by a line.

quote: A lane detection system... uses the principle of Hough transform and Canny edge detector to detect lane lines.

claim: Emergency lane keeping (ELK) systems apply corrections when a vehicle drifts beyond a solid lane marking.
quote: The emergency lane keeping applies correction to a vehicle which drifts beyond a solid lane marking.

claim: Lateral support systems (LSS) aim to prevent crashes caused by lane departure.
quote: The goal of the lateral support systems (LSS) is to help to avoid such crashes.

quote: The perception module ingests and processes data from various sensors, such cameras , LIDAR , RADAR , and ultrasonic SONAR.

claim: The localization module uses 3D point cloud data, GPS, IMU, and mapping information.
quote: The localization module uses 3D point cloud data, GPS , IMU , and mapping information to determine the vehicle's precise position.

claim: The planning module computes actions such as velocity and steering angle outputs.

claim: Modern autonomous driving systems use sensor fusion to improve accuracy and reliability.
